name: sdg03
title: SDG 3: Good health and well-being (Municipal Atlas of the SDGs 2020)
description: The SDG 3 (Good health and well-being) index of the Municipal Atlas of the Sustainable Development Goals in Bolivia 2020 (SDSN Bolivia) and the 9 indicators behind it, for Bolivia's 339 municipalities, with the Atlas population and urbanization rate as context. Each variable is stored at its own reference year, so the panel is sparse: a variable has values only in its year. The index is stored at 2018, the latest reference year of its indicators.

geo:citation: GeoDevelopment Observatory of Bolivia (2026). SDG 3: Good health and well-being, from the Municipal Atlas of the SDGs 2020 (339 municipalities). https://github.com/quarcs-lab/geo4bolivia/blob/main/docs/datasets/sdg03.md
geo:notes: Reference years come from the variable labels. Indicators averaged over a period are stored at its midpoint, rounded down (e.g. average 2014–17 at 2015); the period is given in the description and `geo:year` holds the year used.
The SDG 3 index (`index_sdg3`) summarises indicators from different years; it is stored at 2018, the latest of them.
Load one indicator with its year, e.g. `geo.load("sdg03", variables="index_sdg3", years=2018)`, or every variable as a cross-section with `geo.load("sdg03").groupby("geo_id").first()`.

Most indicators are rates, shares or indices, so their aggregation rule is `none`. Population-weighted averages can be built with the `pop` dataset, which covers every reference year: `geo.aggregate(df, to="department", rules={"index_sdg3": "weighted_mean:pop"}, weights=geo.load("pop"))`.

In DS4Bolivia the rows of three homonym pairs (San Javier in Beni and Santa Cruz, El Puente in Tarija and Santa Cruz, Santa Rosa in Beni and Pando) are attached to the other polygon of the pair. Here the indicators are linked by INE code (`mun_id`), so each lies in its correct municipality; see raw/README.md.
`population_2020` is the Atlas (INE-based) population and differs from the gridded `pop` dataset.

resources.name: sdg03-municipality
resources.geo:source_geometry: Municipal statistics of the Atlas, linked by INE municipality code

fields.name: geo_id
fields.title: Municipality ID
fields.description: GDO-Bolivia municipality geo ID (BO-DD-PP-MM) of the 339-unit municipality map, numbered as in GADM 4.1; its boundary in geo/boundaries/ comes from geoBoundaries (GeoBolivia, public domain). It nests by prefix into the department (BO-DD) and province (BO-DD-PP) IDs; department and province numbers follow GADM order and differ from INE codes.

fields.name: year
fields.title: Year
fields.description: Reference year of the values in the row. Each SDG Atlas variable is stored only at its own reference year (geo:year); indicators averaged over a period are stored at the period's midpoint, rounded down, and the goal index at the latest reference year of its indicators, so the panel is sparse.

fields.name: mun_id
fields.title: INE municipality code
fields.description: Official municipality code of the National Statistics Institute (INE), DDPPMM (department, province, municipality) stored as an integer without the leading zero (e.g. 20101 = La Paz). The Atlas indicators are linked to geo_id through this code, which places DS4Bolivia's three swapped homonym pairs in their correct municipality.

fields.name: index_sdg3
fields.title: Good health index (0-100)
fields.description: SDG 3 (Good health and well-being) index of the Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020, on a 0-100 scale where 100 means the goal's targets are met (best value) and 0 the worst situation. Following the global SDG Index method (Lafortune et al., 2018), each of its 9 indicators is rescaled linearly to 0-100 between a worst value (generally the 2.5th-percentile tail of the municipal distribution) and a best value (the SDG target where one exists, otherwise the average of the five best municipalities, or expert judgement), with the direction set so that higher is always better and values beyond the bounds capped at 0 or 100; the index is the simple (equal-weight) mean of the available rescaled indicators. Components: Institutional birth coverage (%); Infant mortality (per 1,000 births); Under-5 mortality (per 1,000 births); Chagas infestation (% of dwellings); Dengue incidence (per 10,000); Malaria incidence (per 1,000); Tuberculosis incidence (per 100,000); HIV incidence (per million); Adolescent fertility (per 1,000 women). The components refer to different years; the observatory stores the index at 2018, the latest reference year among them.
fields.geo:source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

fields.name: sdg3_1_idca
fields.title: Institutional birth coverage (%)
fields.description: Percentage of births attended in a health facility, average of 2008-2012, the official INE indicator computed from the 2012 Population and Housing Census (INE). Stored at 2010, the period midpoint. In the SDG 3 index it is normalised linearly between 15.7 (worst; 2.5th-percentile tail) and 100 (best; leave no one behind), values beyond the bounds capped.
fields.geo:source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

fields.name: sdg3_2_imr
fields.title: Infant mortality (per 1,000 births)
fields.description: Infant mortality rate: deaths before the first birthday per 1,000 live births, 2016; official municipal estimates by UDAPE (2018). In the SDG 3 index it is normalised linearly between 60 (worst; 2.5th-percentile tail) and 12 (best; SDG target 3.2), values beyond the bounds capped.
fields.geo:source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

fields.name: sdg3_2_mrc
fields.title: Under-5 mortality (per 1,000 births)
fields.description: Under-five mortality rate: deaths before age 5 per 1,000 live births, 2016; official municipal estimates by UDAPE (2018). Correlation with infant mortality is 0.99; the Atlas keeps both, which gives child mortality double weight in the SDG 3 index. In the SDG 3 index it is normalised linearly between 80 (worst; 2.5th-percentile tail) and 25 (best; SDG target 3.2), values beyond the bounds capped.
fields.geo:source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

fields.name: sdg3_3_cdir
fields.title: Chagas infestation (% of dwellings)
fields.description: Chagas vector infestation rate: percentage of dwellings infested, 2017, from the National Chagas Programme of the Ministry of Health (data shared via the National Health Information System, SNIS). In the SDG 3 index it is normalised linearly between 10.4 (worst; 2.5th-percentile tail) and 0 (best; SDG target / average of the top 5), values beyond the bounds capped.
fields.geo:source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

fields.name: sdg3_3_di
fields.title: Dengue incidence (per 10,000)
fields.description: Dengue cases per 10,000 inhabitants in 2018, from the National Dengue-Chikungunya-Zika Control and Prevention Programme of the Ministry of Health (SNIS). In the SDG 3 index it is normalised linearly between 4.89 (worst; 2.5th-percentile tail) and 0 (best; SDG target / average of the top 5), values beyond the bounds capped.
fields.geo:source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

fields.name: sdg3_3_imr
fields.title: Malaria incidence (per 1,000)
fields.description: Annual malaria cases per 1,000 inhabitants, average of 2014-2017, from the National Malaria Programme of the Ministry of Health (SNIS). Stored at 2015. In the SDG 3 index it is normalised linearly between 25.8 (worst; 2.5th-percentile tail) and 0 (best; SDG target / average of the top 5), values beyond the bounds capped.
fields.geo:source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

fields.name: sdg3_3_ti
fields.title: Tuberculosis incidence (per 100,000)
fields.description: Incidence of tuberculosis in all its forms (new cases and relapses) per 100,000 inhabitants in 2017, from the National Tuberculosis Programme of the Ministry of Health (SNIS). In the SDG 3 index it is normalised linearly between 158.7 (worst; 2.5th-percentile tail) and 0 (best; SDG target / average of the top 5), values beyond the bounds capped.
fields.geo:source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

fields.name: sdg3_3_hivi
fields.title: HIV incidence (per million)
fields.description: Annual new HIV cases per 1,000,000 inhabitants, average of 2014-2017 (averaged because cases are few), from the National STI/HIV/AIDS and Viral Hepatitis Programme of the Ministry of Health (SNIS). Stored at 2015. In the SDG 3 index it is normalised linearly between 416.7 (worst; 2.5th-percentile tail) and 0 (best; SDG target / average of the top 5), values beyond the bounds capped.
fields.geo:source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

fields.name: sdg3_7_afr
fields.title: Adolescent fertility (per 1,000 women)
fields.description: Births per 1,000 women aged 15-19, average of 2008-2012, computed from the 2012 Population and Housing Census (INE) as described in Branisa et al. (2016). Stored at 2010, the period midpoint. In the SDG 3 index it is normalised linearly between 156.7 (worst; 2.5th-percentile tail) and 0 (best; leave no one behind), values beyond the bounds capped.
fields.geo:source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

fields.name: population_2020
fields.title: Population (persons)
fields.description: Estimated municipal population in 2020 (persons), as printed in the Atlas municipal profiles ("Población estimada, 2020"). The Atlas does not name the source; the 339 values sum to 11,633,371, exactly INE's 2020 national population projection (Revisión 2020 series), so they are presumably INE's municipal projections. Not an input of any goal index. Differs from the gridded WorldPop-based pop dataset.
fields.geo:source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

fields.name: urbano_2012
fields.title: Urbanization rate (%)
fields.description: Share of the municipal population living in urban areas in 2012 (%), as printed in the Atlas municipal profiles ("Tasa de urbanización, 2012"), from the 2012 Population and Housing Census (INE). INE counts as urban the localities with 2,000 or more inhabitants, which is why 175 municipalities have a rate of 0. Not an input of any goal index (the Atlas treats 15 almost fully urban municipalities as having no applicable farm indicators for SDG 2; 11 of them are 95% or more urban by this rate, while Sucre, Tiquipaya and Potosí are 91–92% and Yunguyo de Litoral 0%).
fields.geo:source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020
